#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 -t 4h --job-name=cifar-resnet --output=myjob.out script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (from --nodes=1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (implicit, not specified in original)
# -c 4         : 4 cores per task (from --cpus-per-task=4)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from --gres=gpu:1)
# -t 4h        : 4 hour walltime (from --time=04:00:00)
# --job-name=cifar-resnet : job name (from --job-name cifar-resnet)
# --output=myjob.out : output file (from --output=myjob.out)
#
# Note: Flux time format uses h for hours (4h = 4 hours)

# Original Slurm output: myjob.out
# Flux: --output=myjob.out (specified at submission)

# Original Slurm nodes: 1
# Flux: -N 1

# Original Slurm GPU: gpu:1
# Flux: -g 1
# Note: Flux GPU allocation does not support GPU type specification
# Performance impact: Cannot specify GPU model/type, will get any available GPU

# Original Slurm cpus-per-task: 4
# Flux: -c 4

# Original Slurm time: 04:00:00 (4 hours)
# Flux: -t 4h or -t 240m or -t 14400s

# Original Slurm job name: cifar-resnet
# Flux: --job-name=cifar-resnet (specified at submission)

module load anaconda
module load use.own
conda env remove --name d22env
conda create --name d22env python=3.11 jupyter pytorch torchvision matplotlib pandas -y
source activate d22env
conda info --envs
echo -e "module loaded"

# Complete submission command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 4 -g 1 -t 4h --job-name=cifar-resnet --output=myjob.out script.sh

issues: The script correctly specifies resource requirements for Flux: 1 node, 1 task, 4 cores per task, 1 GPU, and 4-hour time limit.
Resource specifications are properly documented and match the conversion from Slurm to Flux.
The conversion correctly notes that Flux GPU allocation (-g 1) does not support GPU type specification, which was not present in the original Slurm script anyway.

However, the conda environment setup has a potential issue: 'conda env remove --name d22env' will fail if the environment doesn't exist (first run), but this won't cause the job to fail due to bash's default error handling. Consider adding '|| true' or checking if env exists first.
The 'source activate d22env' command is deprecated; modern conda uses 'conda activate d22env'. This may cause issues depending on the conda version.
The script creates a new conda environment every time it runs, which is inefficient and time-consuming. Consider creating the environment once and reusing it.
No error handling is present. If any module load or conda command fails, the script will continue executing, potentially leading to unexpected behavior.
The 4-hour time limit may be insufficient for creating a conda environment and installing all packages (pytorch, torchvision, etc.), especially on slow filesystems or busy nodes.
No actual work is performed in the script after environment setup. The script only loads modules and creates an environment, then exits.
